chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said:

The man gives the Adhan while sitting, but he does not give the Iqamah except while standing. And he said: 'You give the Adhan while riding, but you do not give the Iqamah except while on the ground.'

key_terms.يُؤَذِّنُ: He gives the Adhan (call to prayer)
key_terms.يُقِيمُ: He gives the Iqamah (second call to prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can the Adhan be given while sitting or riding, and must the Iqamah be given while standing?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the practical flexibility of the Adhan, permitting it while seated or riding due to its communicative nature, whereas the Iqamah, being a precursor to the standing prayer, requires the caller to be standing on the ground. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on physical posture as a sign of reverence and readiness for the ritual act itself, distinguishing between the announcement and the immediate preparation for worship.
